prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Dallas. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Dallas for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: call board-certified oral surgeons, board-certified periodontists, or implant-focused prosthodontists in Dallas who offer CBCT-based planning, digital/guided implant placement, and have good patient outcomes, warranties/implant-system transparency, sedation options and clear financing. I can help you find and vet specific offices — do you want me to search the web for current local practices (and do you have a preferred Dallas neighborhood/zip code or insurance)?

If you want to get started now, here’s a practical plan plus exactly what to call and ask so you’ll get the best candidates.

Who to call (types of practices)
- Board-certified oral & maxillofacial surgeons (OMS): best for complex extractions, bone grafts, sinus lifts, sedation/general anesthesia.
- Board-certified periodontists: specialists in implants and bone/tissue health; excellent for single or multiple implants and grafting.
- Prosthodontists (implant-focused): best when complex restorative planning (full-arch work, esthetics) is required.
- Multidisciplinary implant centers that include a surgeon, periodontist and prosthodontist working together.

How to find specific Dallas offices right now
- Use professional directories to locate certified specialists:
  - AAOMS “Find a Surgeon” (for oral surgeons)
  - American Academy of Periodontology directory (for periodontists)
  - AAID (American Academy of Implant Dentistry) “Find an Implant Dentist”
  - ADA “Find a Dentist”
- Cross-check names with local hospital affiliations (UT Southwestern, Baylor University Medical Center Dallas) — affiliation is a good sign.
- Check Google Reviews, Yelp, Healthgrades; focus on comments about implant success, follow-up care, and complications handling.

What to call and ask (phone script — copy/paste)
Hello, my name is [your name]. I’m considering a dental implant and would like a consultation. I have a few questions before making an appointment:
1) Do you place implants in-house, and which specialists perform the surgery (oral surgeon, periodontist)?  
2) Are you board certified (ABOMS, ABP, ABO)?  
3) Do you do CBCT 3D imaging and digital implant planning here?  
4) What implant systems do you use (Nobel, Straumann, Zimmer, etc.)? Do you guarantee the implant or offer a warranty?  
5) Will the restorative dentist (or prosthodontist) coordinate the crown/bridge/overdenture, or do I need a separate provider?  
6) What sedation options do you offer?  
7) What is an estimated cost range for my case (single tooth, bone grafting, sinus lift if needed)?  
8) Do you finance, accept CareCredit, or work with my insurance (ask to verify benefits)?  
9) Can I see before/after photos and patient references for similar cases?  
10) How many implant cases like mine do you place per year?

Red flags to avoid on the call
- No CBCT available or unwillingness to take 3D imaging for implant planning.
- Vague answers about experience, no references or case photos.
- Pressure to place an implant immediately without a proper consultation or imaging.
- Refusal to disclose what implant system they use or who will restore the crown.

What I recommend you call first (priority list)
1) An ABOMS-certified oral & maxillofacial surgery practice in Dallas (for complex cases, grafting, sedation).  
2) A board-certified periodontist with strong implant experience (for site-specific implants and periodontal management).  
3) An implant prosthodontist or restorative dentist who handles implant crowns/bridges or who partners reliably with your surgeon.

If you want, I can:
- Search now and return a short list (3–6) of specific Dallas practices with phone numbers, addresses, and quick notes on credentials and patient reviews — tell me your ZIP or neighborhood and whether you prefer oral surgeons vs periodontists or have insurance constraints.
- Or I can evaluate 2–3 practices you already found and tell you which looks best based on credentials, reviews, and services.

Which would you prefer?
